```
  chosen. The limit dates from an earlier, approximate method, whose runs
  differed by about 0.04% in the alveolar concentration and by more in mixed
  venous. The check also requires each gap between runs to stay below 1e-14 as

```

[2] rewrite

```
- **How to change the release check's limits.** A fork with an approximate
  method fails 1e-14 even when its arithmetic is correct: a first-order method
  shows gaps near 1.4e-11. Relax 1e-14, and 0.5% becomes the working check. Set
  it above the method's own gaps at the check's step lengths and below a
  difference that a learner could see. The constants are in
  `tests/reference/test_sevo_patient.py`.
```

[3] rewrite

```
**The release check on step length, and why it allows a 0.5% difference.** The
model advances in fixed steps of 0.1 s, and a shorter step should give almost the
same result. Before each release, a test reruns the first minute of the default
sevoflurane induction with steps of 0.1 s, 0.05 s and 0.025 s. Each run's
alveolar, vessel-rich and mixed-venous concentrations must be within 0.5% of the
run with the next shorter step. The 0.5% was set for the simulator's earlier
calculation method, at about ten times the 0.04% alveolar difference that method
showed. The current method's runs agree to better than one part in a trillion
(simulated 2026-10-03), so the much tighter limits above are the ones that would
catch a real error. A compartment that holds almost no agent also passes if its
two values differ by less than 0.000001 vol%, because there a tiny difference
is a large percentage.
```

[4] rewrite

```
The 5e-3 relative tolerance was chosen when the simulator used an earlier
calculation method, the operator split. At that time, the operator split showed
a relative gap of 4e-4 in the alveolar fraction between steps of 0.1 s and
0.025 s, and 5e-3 is about ten times that gap. In the same comparison, the
simulator's current calculation method, the exact step, gives relative gaps of
about 1.4e-13 (simulated 2026-10-03), so the tolerance is kept as a coarse
check. The 1e-8 absolute tolerance lets a negligible difference pass for a
fraction so close to zero that a relative gap means little.
```

[5] rewrite

```
**The release check on step length, and why it allows a 0.5% difference.** The
simulator moves the model forward in fixed time steps, normally 0.1 s long. A
shorter step should give almost the same result. If it does not, the step is too
long. Before each release, a test runs the first minute of the default
sevoflurane induction three times, with steps of 0.1 s, 0.05 s and 0.025 s. In
each run, the alveolar, vessel-rich and mixed-venous concentrations must be
within 0.5% of the run with the next shorter step. The 0.5% limit was set for the
simulator's earlier calculation method. With that method, the alveolar
concentrations of the 0.1 s and 0.025 s runs differed by about 0.04%, so the
limit allowed about ten times that difference. The check compares each run only
with the next shorter step. Under the earlier method, a direct comparison of the
0.1 s run with the 0.025 s run would have failed, because those runs differed by
0.55% in mixed-venous concentration, which has barely begun to rise at one
minute. With the current method, the three runs agree to better than one part in
a trillion (simulated 2026-10-03), so this check is now only a coarse safety net.
The much tighter limit in the paragraphs above is the one that would catch a real
error.

For a compartment that still holds almost no agent, two values also pass if they
differ by less than 0.000001 vol%, one part in a hundred million of the gas. In
such a compartment, a tiny difference can be a large percentage, so a percentage
means little.
```

[6] rewrite

```
**The three agents' dial maxima come from two classes of vaporizer.** The sevoflurane and
isoflurane maxima are those of variable-bypass dials. Desflurane's is the top of the Tec 6's range,
and a Tec 6 is a heated gas–vapour blender. The model fixes ambient pressure at 760 mmHg
(§ "Assumptions"). At that pressure, the same dial setting on either class gives the same partial
pressure, so the model does not need to know which class a limit came from. The classes would
differ only at reduced ambient pressure, which is not modelled (§ "Known limitations").
```

Outline:
- Rows 1-20, one paragraph: the step-length check and its 0.5% limit.
  - The model runs in fixed steps, normally 0.1 s. A shorter step should give almost the same result; if it does not, the step is too long.
  - Before each release, a test runs the first minute of the default sevoflurane induction at 0.1 s, 0.05 s and 0.025 s.
  - Alveolar, vessel-rich and mixed-venous concentrations must be within 0.5% of the next shorter step's run.
  - The 0.5% was set for the earlier method, whose 0.1 s and 0.025 s alveolar values differed by about 0.04%, so the limit allowed about ten times that.
  - Each run is compared only with the next shorter step. A direct 0.1 s to 0.025 s comparison would have failed under the earlier method: 0.55% in mixed-venous concentration, which has barely begun to rise at one minute.
  - The current method's runs agree to better than one part in a trillion (simulated 2026-10-03), so the check is now only a coarse safety net. The tighter limit above is the one that would catch a real error.
  - In a near-empty compartment, a percentage means little. Two values also pass if they differ by less than 0.000001 vol%, one part in a hundred million.

Added words: none. The new paragraph has the same 47 words as the two sentences it replaces.
